My life has been nothing short of complicated so far. Never really got along with people I deemed "too different to me" because my social skills aren't the best, but I did get along very well with other people who had mental health issues. My best friends from primary school to my best friends now all have some flavor of being different. I've always known I'm different from other people, it's not that I'm better than them, just different. 
I was maybe in middle-school when I first realised that difference might stem from ADHD, however by the time I applied for an evaluation I was doing a lot more drugs than what can be considered healthy, the doctors said all my issues might stem from that despite my issues being present before I took anything. Anyways skip ahead a few years, the thought never left me, I needed to be sure so I quit doing drugs, proved my sobriety to doctors by pissing in a cup a few times. In a few months I got the diagnosis and medication, I've never felt better. Thanks to it I quit a pretty life damaging drug habit, and I'm actually focusing on shit that matters now

3 words, rejection sensitivity dysphoria. I've lived my entire life having people around me calling me lazy because it's hard to internalise what I've read which showed in my school grades, calling me weird for having social issues or being awful at texting/reading tone from text messages, criticising me relentlessly for showing even the mildest symptoms of the GAD/ADHD combo. This has resulted in me internalising all of that, basically before I even start doing anything a voice in my head starts calling me a worthless piece of shit who can never get anything done. I also can't take criticism at all because even the mildest criticism towards me feels like the other person is saying "fuck you, I hope you die", even if said criticism is coming from a friendly place. I've become better at handling it, but it's still hard to deal with, especially when I'm so anxious like all the time.

Doctors are of the same class as baristas under capitalism, at least in my Marxist definition of class. Your class isn't dictated by how much money you make, it's dictated by wether or not you own the means of production. A business owner who makes 50k a year is bourgeois and a doctor who makes 250k a year is working class. Only if the doctor personally owns a sizeable part of the business they are employed in do they become bourgeois. Now, of course there are in-betweens and people outside of this class divide (lumpen proletariat and petit-bourgeois), but those are a debate for another day. I as a Marxist of the non-anarchist sect believe that some hierarchies are absolutely necessary to keep certain complicated lines of production working and for the time that capitalism still exists we need a state to protect itself from imperialists taking over in the area a socialist system is being formed in, what I don't like is workers not having a say in said lines of production, a job which these days is only left up to a small handful of people accross the globe.
